newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia and China main market for Kazakh crude.
newsitem.headline: Russia and China main market for Kazakh crude.

text.p: Russia and China are the main future markets for Kazakh crude oil, Kazakh Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin told a news conference on Tuesday.
"China is importing oil today and I'm sure Russia will do the same in 15 years," he said in Moscow. "These are huge territories.
"In three or four years, the world market for us will be Russia and China. And we won't need to seek ports or other outlets."
He did not explain how the former Soviet republic planned to sell crude oil to its big northern neighbour, Russia.

Kazakhstan and Russia have both said this year that they are eyeing Chinese and South Asian oil markets via possible Trans-Asian and Trans-Siberian pipelines in a strategy which could put them in competition with each other.

Kazhegeldin said Almaty had not yet chosen a winner from a shortlist of Amoco Corp, Chinese National Petroleum Corp and Petronas to develop its second-largest oilfield, Uzen. Sources close to the tender said a decision may be taken this week.

He did not say how Almaty planned to widen its oil export capabilities, including routes for Uzen oil, but said the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) project connecting Kazakhstan's Tengiz field to Russia's Black Sea oil export outlet Novorossiisk would help.
His spokesman Amirzhan Kosanov said Kazakh Oil and Gas Minister Nurlan Balgimbayev was in Moscow for talks on CPC, but gave no details.
CPC is the first of several proposed export pipelines that will be needed to carry future Kazakh and other Caspian regions' crude oil output to Western and possibly Asian markets.

Kazakhstan has 700 million tonnes of proven recoverable onshore crude oil reserves, according to British Petroleum's 1996 Statistical Review of World Energy. Reserves in its continental shelf are estimated at 10 billion tonnes.

Kazakhstan produced 20.5 million tonnes (440,000 barrels per day) of oil in 1995, but has been hampered by a lack of export routes. Russia allots it an export quota of about 70,000 barrels per day through the Russian pipeline system.
